title: Here are the coolest e-motorcycles and gear we saw at EICMA 2026
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Micah Toll
| Nov 13 2026 - 7:39 am PT
Customized version of the LiveWire S4 Honcho displayed at EICMA 2026
Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase. That means that all of the newest electric motorcycle announcements happen in one place, and we get a chance to check out the coolest developments and most interesting new gear.
Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.
LiveWire shows off Honcho S4 in several variants, plus new DUST Moto dirt e-bikes
LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its
most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet
, showing just how far the company has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
The new S4 Honcho family was a major focus, including the street-oriented Honcho Street, off-road Honcho Trail, and newly unveiled Honcho Skate, a stripped-down addition to the modular platform. The booth also included LiveWire’s larger S2 electric motorcycles, creating a pretty broad spectrum from lightweight urban machines up through full-size highway-capable electric motorcycles.
A Skate variant of the Honcho shows what a stripped down mini-moto from LiveWire might look like
The other big piece of the booth was DUST Moto, which
LiveWire acquired earlier this year.
The production-intent DUST Hightail was displayed alongside the newly revealed DUST Spur, giving LiveWire an immediate presence in the increasingly popular lightweight electric dirt bike category.
Add in STACYC’s electric balance bikes for young riders, and the entire booth almost looked like an electric two-wheeler progression chart: start a kid on a STACYC, move up through lightweight DUST and Honcho machines, and eventually graduate to a full-size LiveWire.
GRIT motorcycles shows off three models
GR1T Motorcycles is a relatively young European electric motorcycle startup that caught my eye at EICMA with its G1 platform, a lightweight electric motorcycle designed and engineered in Italy. The basic recipe is pretty compelling: 130 km/h (81 mph) top speed, 11 kW of continuous power and 26.6 kW (36 hp) peak, all while weighing just 130 kg (287 lb).
Perhaps most importantly for urban riders, its roughly 6 kWh battery is actually split into two removable 3 kWh packs, meaning apartment dwellers can pull the batteries out and charge them inside. They’re big, but removing them is doable.
GR1T’s bikes therefore pack in around 50% more battery capacity than most electric motorcycles in this size and weight class, meaning roughly 50% more range, as well.
There are also some interesting and clever design choices, like the underslung rear suspension and the triple-camera system that includes front and rear dashcams plus a cockpit-facing camera for recording the rider.
The clever part of the overall design scheme is that GR1T isn’t developing a separate platform for every motorcycle. The same basic G1 chassis, motor, batteries, belt drive, and electronics underpin four versions: the G1S Street, G1X Scrambler, G1XR Raider, and utility-oriented G1M Mission.
Prices are set to start at €8,495 including VAT, putting these squarely in that emerging category of reasonably affordable, lightweight electric motorcycles that have enough speed for real-world commuting without chasing superbike performance.
There’s an important caveat, though: these aren’t production motorcycles yet. GR1T says it is
currently fundraising
, with factory development and pre-orders set to follow after funding closes and first deliveries now targeted for the first half of 2028.
So the bikes aren’t quite ready for primetime yet, but it’s definitely a company to watch.
Real Motors Project Ares
Real Motors brought one of the more visually striking electric motorcycles to EICMA with Project: ARES, a futuristic electric café racer that the American startup describes as an “Electric Analog” machine – basically an attempt to preserve the raw, mechanical connection of motorcycling while ditching unnecessary screens and gadgetry.
And there’s plenty of performance underneath the sci-fi bodywork: Real Motors lists a 75 kW (100 hp) motor, a 15 kWh battery, a 120 mph (192 km/h) top speed, and an estimated weight of 485 lb (220 kg).
The analog analogy is spot on, with the display probably the simplest and most straightforward I’ve ever seen on an electric motorcycle. There’s also no app, no subscription, and no digital handcuffs. The bike is very much the electric equivalent of a simple ICE bike that just rides, albeit with a much nicer ride.
Unlike many of the futuristic concepts scattered around EICMA, ARES is actually headed toward limited production.
Real Motors plans to build just 250 examples in its first LOT 01 production run, with pricing starting at $20,000 and North American deliveries targeted for early 2027. European deliveries are expected after homologation is completed.
The company has also brought former LiveWire CTO Vance Strader onto the project as it makes the difficult transition from a very cool prototype into an actual production motorcycle.
I actually had the chance to do a spin on the bike, and so I’ll be reporting back on the experience. But you can tell from my smile below that the ride was quite an experience!
Big thanks to CEO and Co-founder Trent Dingman for letting me borrow his helmet and the jacket off his back!
Seatylock has the most angle-grinder proof U-Lock for motorcycles
Seatylock has been my go-to e-bike lock company for several years now, and
I use their locks
for my several e-bikes and my wife’s e-bike too.
Now Seatylock has returned with some even more impressive locks. The company showed off its new Ultra D28 lock, which is both angle grinder-proof and wide enough to lock the wheel of a motorcycle. It solves the problem of how do you make a lock strong enough for a motorcycle but also small and light enough that you can actually carry it with you, unlike a massive chain lock that usually stays where you park your motorcycle overnight.
In the image below, you can see the shackle next to an exposed section demonstrating the diamond coating that essentially destroys angle grinder discs – even diamond coated discs.
Multiple sizes offer protection for motorcycle and bicycle wheels, plus there’s a ground anchor with the same angle grinder-proof material
The company also has a slightly smaller version of the same lock designed for bicycles.
Both will absolutely destroy even the toughest angle grinder discs. Sure, eventually someone could cut through them, but it may take a dozen discs and by that point the thief has moved on to an easier target.
Flying Flea
At EICMA 2026, Royal Enfield continued expanding its electric motorcycle ambitions with its
Flying Flea sub-brand
, showcasing the scrambler-style motorcycle alongside its growing lineup of lightweight, retro-inspired electric motorcycles.
There were several interesting colorways and customized designs on display, showcasing the Flying Flea’s stylish design.
The new models blend Royal Enfield’s classic design heritage with modern electric technology, targeting urban riders and those looking for a fun, approachable electric motorcycle rather than a high-performance machine.
With distinctive styling, compact proportions, and an emphasis on accessible riding, the Flying Flea lineup represents Royal Enfield’s effort to carve out a place in the emerging market for smaller electric motorcycles while maintaining the character that has made its gasoline-powered bikes so popular.
Yamaha NMAX E
Yamaha showed off its
new NMAX E electric scooter
, bringing battery-powered performance to one of the brand’s most recognizable urban scooter families.
Designed as an electric alternative to the popular gasoline-powered NMAX, the new model combines familiar sporty styling with a quiet, low-maintenance electric drivetrain aimed at everyday city commuting.
The NMAX E uses Yamaha’s new compact eAxle powertrain, shared with the larger-wheeled XENTER E, and delivers up to 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power, putting it in the 125cc-equivalent class.
With its practical step-through design, automatic operation, and approachable performance, the NMAX E represents another step in Yamaha’s push to electrify its urban mobility lineup, particularly in European markets where scooters are already a popular alternative to cars.
Segway safety scooters
Segway showed off
a new vision
for safer electric scooters, including its futuristic X Cruiser concept that takes rider protection to a whole new level.
Rather than relying solely on traditional motorcycle safety equipment, the X Cruiser explores automotive-inspired features such as integrated seats with seatbelts, partial enclosures, and even a fully roofed version designed to offer additional protection from the elements.
The concept includes several configurations, ranging from a more conventional open scooter to a partially enclosed design and a fully covered model that looks like a cross between a motorcycle and a tiny electric car. While these designs are still concepts rather than production-ready scooters, they demonstrate how Segway is rethinking two-wheeled transportation by exploring ways to make electric scooters safer, more comfortable, and potentially more appealing to riders who might otherwise be hesitant to trade four wheels for two.
Eli Zero gets even faster – and more racecar-like!
Eli Electric Vehicles took to EICMA 2026 to display its compact Eli Zero electric quadricycle, a tiny two-seat urban EV designed to offer much of the convenience of a car without the size, weight, or expense of a conventional automobile.
With its enclosed cabin, side-by-side seating, and ultra-compact footprint, the Eli Zero offers a practical alternative to larger vehicles for short city trips, combining the weather protection and comfort of a car with the maneuverability and efficiency of a much smaller vehicle.
The company revealed a more powerful L7e-class version of the Eli Zero
that it had previously teased,
expanding the vehicle’s capabilities beyond its existing L6e configuration. The new Race Edition also pushes the envelope farther with custom interior and a few extra accents to the body.
With growing interest in smaller, more efficient urban transportation, Eli’s presence at EICMA definitely underlined how the show is increasingly embracing electric mobility solutions that go beyond traditional motorcycles and scooters.
NIU e-scooters get MY27 updates
NIU showed off its latest lineup of electric scooters, continuing the brand’s push to make battery-powered two-wheelers a practical alternative to gasoline-powered urban transportation. Known for its sleek designs, connected technology, and approachable electric scooters, NIU highlighted models aimed at a range of riders, from everyday city commuters to those looking for more powerful machines capable of keeping up with faster urban traffic.
The company showed off several new models for the 2027 model year, with scooters that combine modern styling with features such as smartphone connectivity, smart security systems, and efficient electric drivetrains, all while maintaining the simplicity and low operating costs that make electric scooters so appealing.
While I didn’t see anything groundbreaking at the brand’s booth this year, the incremental updates look to push new tech features further throughout the brand’s many models, helping more of NIU’s offerings enter that premium level that the company has been known for.
Honda EV Outlier is extra futuristic
For something a bit wilder, Honda shared its
futuristic EV Outlier Concept
, an electric motorcycle that explores what two-wheeled design could look like when engineers are freed from the constraints of traditional gasoline-powered motorcycles.
With its long, low-slung profile, radically different riding position, and futuristic bodywork, the EV Outlier looks more like something out of a science fiction movie than a conventional motorcycle. The concept features electric motors integrated into both wheels, giving it two-wheel drive while opening up new possibilities for packaging and weight distribution.
Rather than simply replacing a combustion engine with a battery and motor, Honda used the EV Outlier to rethink the entire motorcycle layout, demonstrating how electrification could lead to entirely new types of riding experiences.
While the bike remains a design concept with no announced production plans, it offers an intriguing glimpse into Honda’s vision for the future of electric motorcycles.
Vespa Elettrica is getting removable batteries
Vespa showed off its next-generation electric scooter lineup at EICMA, including electric versions of the Primavera, Sprint S, and Primavera Tech. While they don’t look radically different, there’s a lot more happening underneath the familiar steel bodywork.
A new Italian-made, rare-earth-free electric motor improves efficiency and performance, while the 45 km/h Primavera and Sprint S now feature removable batteries.
The faster 67 km/h Primavera Tech gets up to 90 km of WMTC range – a 12.5% improvement – along with an updated vehicle management system and more efficient charger.

title: Meta to deploy 25 electric semi trucks across I-10 corridor, but has nothing to ship
content:
Commercial EVs
Electric Semi Truck
Business
Jo Borrás
| Nov 13 2026 - 7:34 am PT
Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta
be shipping any products.
The second major trucking deal between Facebook parent company Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 new battery-electric semis on I-10,
running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona
. But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.
“Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, said Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”
Meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation
(GMA) buyers’ alliance.
The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May
. This new Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.
How the certificates work
ZETc explainer; via CCJ.
This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The company adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy new trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”
Nevoya expects Meta’s fresh batch of semis to begin prowling I-10 in 2027, where they’ll cover approximately 4 million freight miles annually.

title: Tesla kills $41,990 Model Y AWD: all-wheel drive now costs $8,000 more
content:
Fred Lambert
| Nov 13 2026 - 7:32 am PT
Tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator. The cheapest dual-motor Model Y you can order now is the Model Y Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump.
The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla launched it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the company.
What’s left in the Model Y lineup
Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):
Model Y Rear-Wheel Drive: $39,990 (348 miles EPA, 0-60 mph in 6.8 seconds)
Model Y Premium Rear-Wheel Drive: $45,990 (355 miles, 5.4 seconds)
Model Y Premium All-Wheel Drive: $49,990 (327 miles, 4.3 seconds)
Model Y Performance: $57,990
Model Y L Premium (six seats): $61,990
Tesla’s US Model Y configurator on November 13, 2026. The only AWD options left start at $49,990. (Source: Tesla)
Tesla launched the base Model Y AWD in February
, it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.
And the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.
Add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.
Rivals still sell AWD crossovers for about $40,000
The timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.
Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.
If you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a new Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.
This is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk
killed the Model S and Model X in January
to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent new Tesla is the
$61,990 Model Y L
, which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.
Electrek’s Take
We liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.
Now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.
There are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.
And Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.
That’s a problem for a company whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.
How long before the $39,990 RWD goes the same way?

title: Zonveer ZX3 review: one of the best-value electric dirt bikes for beginners
content:
Fred Lambert
| Nov 13 2026 - 6:06 am PT
The Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.
For that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.
Zonveer ZX3 specs and price
Zonveer is a young brand. It launched in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its
EU store
Screenshot
Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to
Zonveer’s product page
Motor: 2,800W peak rear hub motor (2,000W rated), 110 Nm of torque
Top speed: 37 mph, with 20 mph and 28 mph modes
Battery: 48V 25Ah (1,200Wh), removable
Claimed range: 40 to 45 miles on throttle, up to 65 miles with pedal assist
Weight: 130 lb (59 kg), with a 265 lb max load
Brakes: dual hydraulic disc brakes front and rear, 220 mm rotors
Wheels and suspension: 19-inch off-road tires, dual hydraulic suspension front and rear
Charging: about 6 hours on the included 4A charger
Price: $1,799 list, now $1,299 on sale
A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.
Fun first, and built for lighter riders
Zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:
With 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.
My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.
And while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.
Range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.
Black Friday deal
Zonveer’s
Black Friday sale
has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the company gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.
The sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full
refund policy
Electrek’s Take
We’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.
It’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

title: Review: Engwe's M20 3.0 is a 60V Super73 killer at a fraction of the price
content:
Seth Weintraub
| Nov 13 2026 - 5:32 am PT
Engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its
value e-bikes
ower-than-believable prices
. But lately, the brand is climbing the value chain with impressive e-bikes that aren’t just great value but also pack
strong specs
impressive features
Engwe M20 3.0
is a great example…
The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike
released in 2023
Top speed in unlocked off-road mode, hitting 0–15 mph in 2.15 seconds. With heavier riders, expect a few mph less
Peak torque output from the 750W-rated (3300W peak) rear hub motor. You read that right. They are saying a 3.3kW motor is rated at the legal 750W. Why not at this point? Everything is 750W!
180 miles:
Maximum claimed pedal-assist range with the dual 60V 20Ah (2,400Wh) battery setup, dropping to roughly 85 miles on throttle alone. I rode about 40 miles for this review, and the battery just lost 1 bar.
2 hours:
Time to charge a single battery from 0% to 80% using the included 8A fast charger. A little math tells us the full story. 60V*8A = 480W. 480Wx2 hours = 960Wh. You still have another half hour of charging to get the the full 1.2kWh.
102 lbs:
Total curb weight, paired with a 330-pound maximum payload capacity. Heavier riders will push that to the limit if they have passengers.
$1,399–$1,699:
Typical retail pricing depending on battery configuration and current sales. We have 10% off code ELECTREKCO
which brings it all the way down to $1259
The M20 is fairly easy to assemble. At just over 100lbs, it is a bit hard to move around, but once assembled, it feels like a pretty impressive piece of machinery. I love the street tires on here instead of pretending to be an off-roader. Dual bright headlights and brake light with turn signals really give this thing some street cred. Adding to the safety roster, Engwe upgraded the quad-piston brakes with sporty red calipers and 202 mm rotors. This is not a value bike. The rear suspension is tight, which is great for 2 riders but might feel stiff out of the box for light riders. The seat is *chef’s kiss* even for 2 riders. Very soft and comfortable but not too soft. It even has a little ‘gas tank’ storage area aft the seat, which is keyed and enough to hold a few sandwiches, some riding gloves, or a small purse.
One gripe: There are 3 sets of keys on here, the aforementioned storage area and one set each for each battery. We’d love to see these things keyed together.
The bike/moped/moto came with a huge 1.2 kW battery (or 2 in our case – unless you have a 80-mile commute, 1 should be plenty) that must be charged individually. But with a 60V 8A charger, each one only takes about 2-3 hours to charge, which is impressive.
The Engwe M20 ride
I did not expect to like the ride of this thing as much as I did. We can dispense with the pleasantries here; it came set to Class 2 mode with a 20mph top speed and stickers to match; a quick Google search will show you how to open this up to 40mph open mode. I take responsibility for my own actions.
The first thing you’ll notice here is that the motor is whisper-quiet, and with the street tires, there is very little road noise, even at 35mph. The half throttle is plenty responsive, a lot more so than the cadence sensor on the pedals, which are vestigial at best here. Those big brakes are a bit softer than I’d prefer, but given a good squeeze, those 203mm rotors and quad-piston hydraulic brakes are going to stop you, the 100lb bike, and your passenger/cargo fairly quickly.
The cops
My girlfriend and I got pulled over for the first time in my e-biking life as I was picking her up at the coffee shop. The cop was immediately apologetic because “he thought we were kids” and not the 50-year-olds under the helmets he encountered. Then he noticed the pedals and said that we’re all clear and that what we were on looked like a motorcycle and that a couple of e-moto kids had gotten into accidents recently, one hit by a drunk driver and who is still in a coma. While he was already letting us go, I pointed out the Class 2 sticker on the bike, and he gave me the thumbs-up as we sped off at 30mph. This M20 passed the local police test with flying colors. I can’t guarantee you’ll have the same experience in your jurisdiction.
M20 Downsides
Most of my gripes on this e-bike are inherent to the form factor. It is heavy at over 100 lbs, but you’d expect that with a 3.3kW motor, 2.4kW of batteries, and room for two. That said, don’t buy this bike if you need to take it up stairs or plan to pedal it without assist. In fact, this isn’t a bikepath bike or a put it on the back of your car bike. And, don’t buy this bike if you like to pedal. It’s too big and fast. This is a 35 mph roads bike. Also 3 sets of keys?
Electrek’s take:
I did not expect to love this bike as much as I have. It is the perfect train station bike for me, and as a bonus, it is a great way to take my girlfriend to the coffee shop on the weekends. It has fat tires, great suspension, a cushy seat, and strong, smooth acceleration and confidence-inspiring braking. It looks cool enough for the cops to think I’m a kid picking up his girlfriend, and it has so much range that I probably won’t need to charge it monthly. At $1399-$1699 (
) depending on battery config, this is less than half the price of some of the pricier and admittedly more stylish Super73 options out there.
I understand that some will fault Engwe for selling a 3.3kW motor e-bike as a class 2 e-bike. But I genuinely feel safer on the road, being able to go at the 35mph speed that cars are going rather than forcing them to go around me. Plus, it isn’t like every single car on the road goes over the speed limit. So why not bikes too?
The Engwe M20 3.0 is over the limit but in all of the best possible ways.

title: Shinsung E&G unveils 650 W bifacial TOPCon solar modules with 23.25% efficiency - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
South Korean solar manufacturer Shinsung E&G has introduced new n-type TOPCon solar modules for ground-mounted, floating PV and agrivoltaic applications. The bifacial panels feature power outputs ranging from 640 W to 650 W and maximum conversion efficiencies of 23.25%.
Emiliano Bellini
13 Nov 2026
Technology & Products
Commercial & industrial
Utility-scale
South Korea-based solar module manufacturer
Shinsung E&G
has unveiled two new series of bifacial solar modules based on n-type tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon) cell technology.
The new products include the SS-JM-TK series for ground-mounted solar installations and the SS-JM-TN series for floating photovoltaic and agrivoltaic applications. Both product lines are available in three versions, with nominal power outputs of 640 W, 645 W and 650 W.
The modules feature 156 bifacial monocrystalline solar cells and offer conversion efficiencies ranging from 22.89% to 23.25% under standard test conditions (STC).
The ground-mounted modules measure 2,465 mm × 1,134 mm × 30 mm and weigh 33.5 kg. The largest model, the SS-JM650TK, delivers a maximum power output of 650 W and an efficiency of 23.25%. It features an open-circuit voltage of 55.71 V and a short-circuit current of 14.52 A.
Under the manufacturer’s bifacial nominal power irradiance (BNPI) conditions, the ground-mounted series delivers power outputs of 700 W to 710 W, with corresponding efficiencies of up to 25.40%. Actual rear-side power generation depends on ground reflectivity and installation conditions.
The floating PV and agrivoltaic modules have the same length and width but feature a thicker, 35 mm frame. They also weigh 33.5 kg and provide maximum front-side power outputs of 650 W, with efficiencies reaching 23.25%.
Under BNPI conditions, the floating and agrivoltaic series delivers outputs of 705 W to 717 W, with the highest-rated model achieving a bifacial-equivalent efficiency of 25.65%.
Both product lines feature a dual-glass construction comprising 2.0 mm heat-strengthened glass on the front and rear sides, an anodized aluminum alloy frame, and an IP68-rated junction box with three bypass diodes.
The modules are designed for operation at a maximum system voltage of 1,500 V and temperatures ranging from -40 C to 85 C.
According to the manufacturer, the ground-mounted modules have a maximum power temperature coefficient of -0.34%/C, compared with -0.29%/C for the floating and agrivoltaic variants.
The ground-mounted series is rated for mechanical test loads of 5,400 Pa on the front and 2,400 Pa on the rear. The floating and agrivoltaic modules offer a 5,400 Pa test-load rating on both sides.
Shinsung E&G provides a 12-year product warranty and a 30-year performance warranty for both series. The company guarantees at least 99% of the initial power output after the first year and 87.4% after 30 years, with maximum annual degradation of 0.4%.
In August, Shinsung E&G
opened a new 350 MW solar module production line
at its Gimje factory in South Korea, bringing the facility’s total production capacity to 600 MW. The company said the line would manufacture n-type solar modules for projects in the Saemangeum development region, including an 80 MW ground-mounted installation, another 74 MW project and a 300 MW floating solar facility.

title: The Hydrogen Stream: Uniper and VNG Produce first green hydrogen at 30 MW facility in Germany - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
The hydrogen will be transported through a roughly 25 km former natural gas pipeline converted to carry hydrogen, with deliveries to a TotalEnergies’ refinery scheduled to begin in 2027.
Sergio Matalucci
13 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Energy Storage
Hydrogen
Utility-scale
The 30 MW electrolysis plant in Germany
have produced their first green hydrogen at the 30 MW electrolyzer facility at the Bad Lauchstädt Energy Park in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. The facility uses renewable electricity from a connected wind farm and is now entering a testing phase to assess the components of the integrated energy system. The hydrogen will be transported through a roughly 25 km former natural gas pipeline converted to carry hydrogen, with deliveries to TotalEnergies’ refinery in Leuna scheduled to begin in 2027. The project aims to demonstrate an integrated hydrogen value chain combining renewable power generation, electrolysis, storage, pipeline transport, and industrial consumption. Full commissioning is expected in 2027, when the facility is scheduled to begin supplying industrial customers.
Researchers
have assessed potential hydrogen transport corridors connecting West Africa to Europe via existing and planned natural gas pipeline routes, estimating a combined transport capacity of up to 7.16 million metric tons of green hydrogen per year. The study, conducted by Yifei Lu, Abeeb Adekunle Garba, Thiemo Pesch, and Andrea Benigni, examined transport scenarios involving the West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP), Nigeria-Morocco Gas Pipeline (NMGP), Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline (TSGP), and Maghreb-Europe Gas Pipeline (MEGP). The researchers compared a coastal corridor through Morocco and Spain with an inland route through Niger and Algeria, as well as a combined configuration using both corridors. They found that the combined configuration could transport almost twice as much hydrogen as either individual route, requiring a pipeline network spanning approximately 15,082 km and an estimated investment of €25.3 billion. Using a two-stage framework combining mixed-integer linear programming optimization and physical gas network simulations, they also assessed pressure drops, flow velocities, and compression requirements. At operating pressures of 80 bar to 100 bar, the combined configuration would require 34 compressor stations with a total installed capacity of 661 MW. Reducing the minimum operating pressure to 50 bar could increase hydrogen flow velocities to 22.37 m/s, exceeding the assumed nominal design velocity of 15 m/s. In their study, published in the
International Journal of Hydrogen Energy
, the researchers said developing both export corridors could diversify Europe’s renewable hydrogen supply routes. However, they cautioned that the estimated capacity represents a long-term technical planning scenario rather than a deployment forecast, as actual hydrogen availability will depend on regional demand, infrastructure development, investment, and cross-border cooperation.
Hydroplane
will lead the development of a hydrogen fuel cell-powered watercraft designed to transport modular hydrogen tank containers across New York’s inland waterways. The project, supported by the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA), aims to reduce the costs, emissions, and logistical complexity of clean hydrogen distribution across the state. “Hydroplane will lead a consortium that includes Serco North America, Hornblower Group, Pacific Hydrogen, Messer North America, and Unitrove,” the company said.
India’s Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
has agreed to extend the commissioning deadlines for approximately 1.5 GW of subsidized electrolyzer manufacturing capacity awarded under the first tranche of its Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) program, according to
The Economic Times
. The decision affects several manufacturers, including Reliance, Ohmium, and John Cockerill Greenko, which received support under a funding program worth approximately $220 million. The delays reportedly reflect slower-than-expected growth in India’s green hydrogen market, with a lack of confirmed orders and delays in reaching financial close for several hydrogen and green ammonia projects weighing on demand for electrolyzer equipment.

title: Chinese PV Industry Brief: Energy China shortlists 23 module suppliers for 15 GW tender - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
In other news, JinkoSolar has secured certification under new Chinese PV standards and Trina Solar is expanding into AI data center energy solutions, Drinda has canceled its Oman factory project, while GCL SI has secured a module supply contract, and polysilicon oversupply continues to weigh on prices.
Vincent Shaw
13 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Energy China
has shortlisted 23 manufacturers for its 2026 centralized procurement of 15 GW of solar modules, including LONGi, Tongwei, JinkoSolar, JA Solar and Trina Solar. The tender covers 10.7 GW of tunnel oxide passivated contact (TOPCon) modules, 1 GW of heterojunction (HJT) modules and 3.3 GW of back-contact (BC) modules. Shortlisted bids range from CNY 0.695 ($0.102)/W to CNY 0.779/W. The announcement identifies shortlisted bidders, with final contract awards yet to be confirmed.
JinkoSolar
said it is among the first manufacturers to secure certification under two mandatory Chinese national standards: GB 47739-2026, covering PV module safety requirements, and GB 47740-2026, covering PV module nameplate and marking requirements. The certifications were issued by the China Quality Certification Centre (CQC) and China General Certification Center (CGC). The standards introduce stricter requirements for module safety, labeling and manufacturing consistency.
Trina Solar
and Intel showcased an integrated energy and computing solution for artificial intelligence (AI) data centers at the ninth China International Import Expo in Shanghai. Trina Solar presented grid-forming battery energy storage systems, AI-driven energy dispatch technology and an 800 V high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) power supply solution. The companies launched a pilot project in September to coordinate energy supply and computing operations. The collaboration is part of Trina Solar’s expansion into energy infrastructure solutions for AI data centers.
has canceled plans to build a 5 GW solar cell manufacturing facility in Oman, citing escalating international trade tensions, geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East and changes to China’s PV technology export policies. The Chinese solar cell manufacturer said the developments had undermined the project’s viability. Drinda signed a letter of intent with the Oman Investment Authority in June 2024 to develop a 10 GW TOPCon cell manufacturing facility with an estimated investment of $700 million. The project was originally planned in two 5 GW phases.
GCL System Integration (GCL SI)
has secured a module supply contract for a 1 GW solar project developed by Xinjiang Xingqihang New Energy in Wusu, Xinjiang region. The contract covers approximately 776,840 modules rated at 710 W each, representing about 551.6 MW of DC capacity. Final delivery volumes will depend on project implementation. The agreement also includes transportation, installation guidance, technical support and after-sales services.
TrendForce
said China’s polysilicon inventories remained above 570,000 metric tons, while domestic production was expected to fall to approximately 95,000 metric tons in November. Despite further production cuts, polysilicon supply continues to slightly exceed demand from downstream ingot producers. Wafer inventories stood at around 27 GW, while average prices for 183 mm wafers fell to CNY 0.95 ($0.14) per piece. Weak module orders and persistent oversupply continue to put downward pressure on prices across the PV supply chain.

title: Dark clouds gather over Germany’s solar sector - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Solar module prices are stagnating, while battery energy storage system prices are expected to rise for the first time. Germany’s solar market could face significant challenges if policymakers fail to push through reforms to Germany’s Renewable Energy Sources Act (EEG) in time, according to Martin Schachinger of pvXchange.
Martin Schachinger, pvXchange.com
13 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Just as nature often falls calm before a storm, Germany is currently experiencing a period of apparent inactivity, particularly within the governing coalition when it comes to legislative reforms in the energy sector. Instead of swiftly finalizing reforms that would at least avoid undermining the renewable energy sector and secure approval from the relevant authorities, the government appears more focused on making concessions to major players in the fossil fuel industry.
Whether deliberately or through sheer irresponsibility, the federal government is delaying necessary decisions and postponing the finalization of the EEG 2027, Germany’s Renewable Energy Sources Act, and a package of measures concerning the electricity grid. This is fueling uncertainty about the future and threatening the viability of numerous business models and the companies that depend on them. The question is whether this is merely a passing shower or a major storm brewing on the horizon.
Solar module price trends this month, by contrast, resemble a gentle breeze, offering some relief. Price reductions in the Full Black and Mainstream categories have been marginal, while prices in the other two categories have remained unchanged. A slight increase in demand in the second half of the year has been met with generally good module availability. As a result, the market is experiencing neither significant oversupply nor shortages, apart from certain ultra-high-efficiency products. Although the overall trend remains slightly downward, manufacturers are not expected to make any further significant price cuts before the end of the year.
The situation is quite different for energy storage products. For years, battery prices moved in only one direction: downward. Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, in particular, benefited from steadily declining costs thanks to improvements in energy density and economies of scale. However, prices now appear to have reached a floor. Rising energy and transportation costs are prompting manufacturers to introduce significant price increases for the first time. These increases have been announced gradually over recent months, and by January at the latest, products from various brands are expected to cost more than they do today, at least in the residential storage segment. As wholesalers, we are preparing for a sharp increase in demand toward the end of the year.
This tendency to bring forward purchases, along with similar developments, is currently boosting order books across the sector. But how long can this surge last? Until Christmas, or perhaps even into the first quarter of 2027?
A more serious storm is brewing over the European Commission’s state aid approval for the planned reform of Germany’s Renewable Energy Sources Act (EEG). If approval is not secured in time, there is a risk that subsidies for solar power could be suspended from Jan. 1, 2027. The current authorization expires at the end of this year. If the new legislation is not adopted and submitted to the European Commission in time, new solar projects could face considerable legal and investment uncertainty, particularly those that depend on public subsidies or the financial security provided by guaranteed support mechanisms. This would primarily affect medium- and large-scale, debt-financed PV installations, while conventional residential systems designed for self-consumption would be less exposed.
Nevertheless, I believe a market-wide downturn cannot be ruled out. Some competitors I have spoken with are less pessimistic. They point to a growing number of large-scale, subsidy-free solar projects that can operate profitably without EEG support. In the small and medium-sized segments, too, emerging business models and service providers, including those offering direct marketing services, suggest that new installations could remain economically viable.
However, every installation needs a grid connection, and the process of securing one should be as straightforward as possible. Unfortunately, despite the stated political goal of reducing bureaucracy, more and more obstacles are being introduced. These additional requirements impose costs on system operators, potentially making many projects economically unviable.

Martin Schachinger has studied electrical engineering and has been active in the field of photovoltaics and renewable energy for almost 30 years. In 2004, he set up the pvXchange.com online trading platform. The company stocks standard components for new installations and solar modules and inverters that are no longer being produced.

Research & Development
Sodium-ion batteries are approaching lithium-ion performance in key areas, with commercial cells reaching energy densities of 175 Wh/kg and offering strong low-temperature performance. Silvia Bodoardo, professor at the Polytechnic University of Turin, told
pv magazine
that utility-scale energy storage represents the technology’s most promising market, as manufacturers ramp up production.
Sergio Matalucci
13 Nov 2026
Research & Development
Batteries
Energy Storage
Singeng sodium-ion battery project in Hubei
Sodium-ion batteries are emerging as a viable alternative to lithium-ion technology for stationary energy storage, driven by improvements in energy density, cycle life, safety and manufacturability.
According to Silvia Bodoardo, full professor at the Polytechnic University of Turin and scientific representative for the Batteries European Partnership Association (BEPA), the most significant development over the past 12 months has been the growing technological maturity of sodium-ion batteries.
“Sodium-ion technology clearly represents the most important development,” Bodoardo told
pv magazine
. “The fundamental shift is no longer just about material performance, but the convergence of energy density, cycle life, safety, and manufacturability.”
Commercial sodium-ion cells have reached energy densities of around 175 Wh/kg, compared with approximately 205 Wh/kg for advanced lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries. The narrowing gap is particularly relevant for stationary storage, where weight is less critical than in electric vehicles.
“The gap is therefore becoming relatively small for stationary applications, where gravimetric energy density is not the dominant key performance indicator,” said Bodoardo.
Low-temperature performance is another area of progress. CATL’s second-generation sodium-ion technology reportedly operates across a temperature range of -40 C to 70 C, retaining around 90% of its capacity at -40 C.
Cycle life is also improving, with commercial-grade cells demonstrating capacity retention above 95% after 5,000 full-depth cycles, according to Bodoardo.
Beyond sodium-ion, non-lithium battery technologies are increasingly targeting different storage durations rather than competing directly with lithium-ion across all applications.
“The market is starting to split into roughly two- to six-hour batteries and true long-duration energy storage systems,” Bodoardo said.
Vanadium redox flow batteries, for example, are progressing toward installations with capacities of tens or hundreds of megawatt-hours, while gigawatt-hour-scale projects have also been proposed. Zinc-based and iron-air technologies are similarly targeting long-duration applications.
“In short, non-lithium batteries are increasingly differentiating by application, with sodium-ion emerging as a direct competitor to LFP for multi-hour storage, while flow, zinc, and iron-air technologies are increasingly geared toward long-duration storage,” Bodoardo said.
Commercial activity is accelerating, particularly in China.
CATL launched its sodium-ion battery energy storage system (BESS) in June 2026
and expects cumulative shipments of around 1 GWh by the end of the year, with international deliveries scheduled to begin in 2027.
The development marks a significant step for a technology that accounted for less than 1% of global lithium-ion battery production in 2025.
Europe is also making progress. In September 2026, Altris, Clarios and InoBat reported that their European sodium-ion battery platform had successfully completed customer validation.

Markets & Policy
The Norwegian government says the deal, covering 12 million tonnes of emission reductions, will help to accelerate the development of renewable energy sources in Indonesia.
Patrick Jowett
13 Nov 2026
Markets & Policy
Asia-Pacific
Norway has agreed to purchase up to 12 million tonnes of emission reductions from Indonesia via a new carbon credit agreement.
Under the terms of the agreement, set to last ten years according to a statement published by the Norwegian government, Norway will purchase verified emissions reductions generated through new renewable energy projects in Indonesia.
Revenue from the sales “makes it possible for Indonesia to build projects that would otherwise not be realised,” the government’s statement adds.
The agreement was signed by the Global Green Growth Institute, acting on behalf of Norway, and Indonesian state-owned utility PLN.
It operates under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement, which allows countries to cooperate on emissions reductions through the transfer of carbon credits between nations.
The deal builds on a climate cooperation agreement signed by Norway and Indonesia in June last year, which established a framework for using carbon-market financing to support floating solar power plants on reservoirs.
Norway’s Minister of Climate and Environment Sigrun Aasland said the new cooperation will help to ensure that more of Indonesia’s electricity comes from solar rather than coal, which currently covers over 70% of the country’s electricity production.
“[The agreement] shows how international cooperation can contribute to both emission cuts and a faster transition to renewable energy,” Aasland added.
The deal arrives as Indonesia begins implementing a
large-scale solar programme
aiming to deploy
100 GW of solar by 2029
. The country surpassed 1 GW of solar capacity in 2025, with total capacity reaching
Earlier this year, the Norwegian government backed a
carbon finance procurement facility
in Zambia that sees Norway purchase carbon credits generated by renewable energy projects. The project launched with a
300 MW solar tender
for projects connected to on-site storage.

title: Sodium-ion pouch cells target cold-climate industrial niche - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
Grepow has launched five sodium-ion pouch cells from 2 Ah to 7 Ah, aimed at industrial equipment and cold-climate applications that need high pulse power.
Vincent Shaw
13 Nov 2026
Technology & Products
Batteries
Energy Storage
Assembly line of Grepow
Shenzhen-based battery manufacturer Grepow launched the series on Nov. 12, adding sodium-ion as a third core chemistry alongside its established nickel-metal hydride and lithium polymer lines.
The range is aimed at industrial equipment, cold-weather power systems, and specialty applications that require short bursts of high current.
All five models have a nominal voltage of 3.0 V. The four smaller cells, from 2 Ah to 6.5 Ah, have a charge cutoff of 3.4 V, while the 7 Ah flagship is rated to 4.0 V. Under specified lab conditions, the series supports discharge at up to 45C for 30 seconds and pulse discharge at up to 100C for two seconds, the company said.
Winter performance
In Grepow’s internal testing, a cell completed repeated three-second 28C pulse discharges after a four-hour rest at -20 C, and the same protocol at 20C after resting at -30 C. The company said the cells can also sustain continuous 0.2C discharge at -20 C for lower-rate output in prolonged cold.
In a separate internal comparison under selected conditions, Grepow said its sodium-ion cell showed stronger high-rate pulse discharge than a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cell at -20 C. The figures have not been independently verified, and performance will vary with pack design and operating conditions.
On cycle life, Grepow said a development cell retained 94% of its original capacity after 2,000 cycles in internal testing at 25 C with 1C charging and 30C discharging, compared with 83% for an LFP cell in the same test. Based on the current degradation curve, the company projects the cell could exceed 4,000 cycles before falling to 80% capacity.
Its product page states that the 4,000-plus figure is a projection rather than a completed test result, and that actual service life will depend on operating conditions and system design.
Core markets
The pouch format sets the series apart in a sodium-ion market where prismatic cells dominate volume production. Grepow has supplied nickel-metal hydride batteries for nearly three decades and, since 2012, high-rate lithium polymer packs for drones under its Tattu and Gens Ace brands, giving it an existing channel into the specialized, lower-volume markets the new series targets.
The company offers customization in cell selection, pack structure, and battery management systems for non-standard voltage, current, and form-factor requirements.
Grepow cited target applications including cold-weather vehicle starting and jump starters, auxiliary power for construction machinery, backup power for telecom base stations in cold regions, mobile robotics, and small stationary storage. That sets it apart from the large-format prismatic sodium-ion cells in China’s energy storage and electric vehicle pipelines, where cost competition is intensifying.
Whether the industrial pouch-cell segment proves commercially durable will depend on how the cycle-life projection holds up in real-world use and how customers weigh sodium-ion against established LFP options.

title: US firm claims 96,000-wafer-per-hour deposition line for tandem cells - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
NAED Energy Holding has said its new vertical deposition platform is rated at 96,000 wafers per hour and designed to make perovskite-silicon tandem cells targeting 30% efficiency.
Brian Publicover
13 Nov 2026
Technology & Products
tandem cells
Miami-based NAED Energy Holding said its PV-1 PECVD-V, a vertical in-line deposition platform for solar cell manufacturing, is rated at 96,000 wafers per hour, double the 48,000 wafers per hour of its previous XL-class platform.
The platform combines
plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD)
and physical vapor deposition (PVD) on a single shared-carrier line. Wafers travel upright through each stage, and to reach the second side, the entire carrier is lifted and turned 180 degrees rather than the wafers being flipped individually, which NAED said reduces direct wafer handling between process steps.
NAED said the line is designed to produce its T2X two-terminal perovskite/heterojunction (HJT) tandem cell, which targets 30% cell efficiency, and that it plans to sell the cells for terrestrial and space applications alongside glass-glass modules starting at 600 W.
According to the company, six of the line’s 13 process tools are complete and the remaining seven are in production. NAED said it designs the tools in-house, machines them in its own facility in the United States, and is now taking reservations for production tool slots from manufacturers.
“Going vertical let us double throughput and build the line around tandem cells from day one, rather than retrofitting tandem onto a platform designed for something else,” said Malcom Longair, media and development lead at NAED.
Rated figures
NAED said the 96,000 wafers-per-hour figure is a rated throughput and that 30% is a target efficiency, with full specifications and measured station test data available to qualified manufacturers on request. The release does not specify wafer size, yield or uptime, and does not name customers, investors, executives or the location of the production facility.
The company said the line, the carrier-turning mechanism, the wafer-retention carrier and the T2X cell are the subject of pending US patent applications, and that its intellectual property has been appraised at $179 million under an ASC 820 Level 3 fair-value methodology, an accounting standard that values assets using unobservable inputs such as management assumptions. NAED did not name the appraiser.
NAED describes itself as an aerospace, engineering and utility-energy company with operations in South Florida, New York and Nevada and a presence in Indonesia.
Perovskite-silicon tandem cells have already exceeded NAED’s target in the lab. Longi set a
world record of 35.5% efficiency
for a perovskite-silicon tandem cell in July. In the United States, Tandem PV
launched commercial perovskite-silicon manufacturing
in California in April and has since
announced a 30.4%-efficient demonstration module

title: China’s highways could generate 182 TWh of solar annually - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Researchers at China’s Tongji University have developed a framework to assess highway PV potential based on solar irradiance, terrain and road networks. They estimate that China’s highways could generate enough solar power to cover 1.85% of national electricity consumption.
Lior Kahana
13 Nov 2026
Research & Development
Utility-scale
Illustration of roadside PV
A research team at China’s
Tongji University
has developed a new framework to assess the PV generation potential of highway networks. The approach combines solar irradiance, terrain and road-network characteristics and can be adapted to different countries by adjusting its parameters to local conditions.
“This research creates an irradiance-terrain-road network coupling model for highway PV assessment,” corresponding author Xiaojun Shen told
pv magazine
. “Unlike prior studies that only calculate available land, we integrate solar resources, terrain occlusion and road distribution, and categorize highway usable space. Furthermore, we propose three tailored operation schemes for off-grid, weak-grid and strong-grid scenarios, which helps planners match highway PV solutions to local grid conditions.”
The framework estimates annual highway PV generation potential based on solar irradiance, terrain effects and available installation area. It considers three categories of space: roadside areas, including medians and slopes; structural areas at tunnel entrances and exits; and service-area rooftops. The calculations account for installation geometry, module efficiency and system losses. The researchers also proposed three operating strategies: self-consumption with surplus energy storage in off-grid areas, grid support during electricity shortages in weak-grid areas and surplus electricity exports in strong-grid areas.
For the Chinese case study, the researchers used NASA Power irradiance data for 2025, with a spatial resolution of 0.5° × 0.5°, to define four solar-resource zones using ArcGIS. They divided terrain into three elevation categories – above 3,000 meters, between 500 meters and 3,000 meters, and below 500 meters – and assigned correction factors of 0.55, 0.75 and 0.95, respectively. They then used OpenCV to combine the resulting maps with China’s 185,000 km highway network. The calculations assumed a module tilt angle of 35 degrees, median widths of 1.5 meters, roadside slope widths of 5 meters and module efficiency of 17.5%, resulting in an overall conversion efficiency of 13.66% after accounting for losses.
“We were surprised to find that the dense highway network in central and eastern China creates substantial PV potential, even though the solar resource level there is lower than the west,” Shen said. “In addition, terrain shading imposes a dramatic reduction on power output for mountain highways, which is often overlooked in large-scale potential estimates.”
The results showed that China’s 185,000 km highway network has an estimated annual PV generation potential of 182 TWh, equivalent to approximately 1.85% of the country’s total electricity consumption in 2025. Roadside areas account for the largest share of the potential, followed by service-area buildings, while structural areas contribute less than 0.5%.
The researchers identified three major challenges to large-scale highway PV deployment: high installation costs and long payback periods that limit economic viability; potential conflicts with roadside ecology and traffic safety; and fragmented, site-specific demonstration projects that lack coordinated regional planning and systematic operation and maintenance.
“As for follow-up work, we plan to study the techno-economic performance of highway PV-storage configurations in service areas,” Shen said. “Traffic safety constraints for roadside PV installations will also be included to form practical deployment guidance.”
The findings are presented in “
Photovoltaic generation potential assessment of highway systems based on irradiance–terrain–road network coupling
,” published in
Next Energy

title: US tears down 10 historic, highly contaminated Cold War-era buildings
content: Ten historic, heavily contaminated buildings at the heart of Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) have been reduced to rubble. The demolition marks the end of a six-year environmental cleanup campaign.Known collectively as Isotope Row, the tightly packed cluster spanned more than 12,000 square feet across the laboratory’s central campus. Removing the derelict structures eliminates long-standing radiological risks. It also frees up prime real estate for next-generation science.“After decades standing at the heart of ORNL, Isotope Row is gone and ORNL’s skyline is forever changed,” said Clint Wolfley, senior vice president of end state delivery for prime cleanup contractor United Cleanup Oak Ridge (UCOR).Coordinating a delicate teardownThe US Department of Energy’s (DOE) Oak Ridge Office of Environmental Management worked alongside UCOR to execute the project. Preparing the aging complex took six years of meticulous engineering. However, crews demolished the physical buildings in just two months.To keep neighboring laboratories running without disruption, demolition teams limited heavy teardown work to afternoon hours. This schedule required close coordination with laboratory operator UT-Battelle and the DOE’s Office of Science. Workers also disposed of most demolition debris directly on site. This approach spared taxpayers the high cost of hauling contaminated rubble to distant facilities.Isotope Row dates back to the late 1940s through the early 1960s. For decades, scientists inside these buildings produced radioisotopes used in medicine, industry, scientific research, and national defense.Operations shut down in the early 1990s. The facilities were left behind with radioactive isotopes, mercury, asbestos, and contaminated machinery still inside. Before demolition equipment could move in, crews had to sever all utility connections and strip out hazardous insulation. This preparatory phase is known as transitioning the buildings to “cold-and-dark” status.Clearing complex hazardsDeactivation teams entered the buildings in 2020 to tackle the interior hazards step by step. Multidisciplinary workers removed combustible materials, six contaminated hot cells, and several specialized gloveboxes. They also hauled out four 2,000-pound tanks that previously stored inert gas. In total, teams removed nearly three million pounds of waste from the site.The trickiest engineering challenge hung 10 to 15 feet above the laboratory floors. Central ventilation and process off-gas pipes were partly made of a concrete-and-asbestos blend that had soaked up radioactive contamination over decades. Crews used strict containment barriers and specialized packaging to dismantle the overhead ducts without releasing hazardous dust.Federal Project Director Michael Griswold said the project demanded high-level technical skill and an unwavering focus on worker safety.“This accomplishment reduces risks today while opening new opportunities for the laboratory’s tomorrow,” Griswold said.Wolfley credited the cleanup workforce for six years of creative problem-solving. He noted that their efforts have turned one of ORNL’s most hazardous footprints into an asset for future discovery.“After decades standing at the heart of ORNL, Isotope Row is gone and ORNL’s skyline is forever changed, clearing the way for its next generation of scientific discovery,” concluded UCOR.

title: China achieves 99.9999 percent purity in new hydrogen chloride plant
content: A single stray impurity or molecule can ruin an entire batch of microchips. To prevent microscopic defects during fabrication, semiconductor manufacturers use specialty gases refined to near-perfection. China expanded its supply of this key material in a push to localize chipmaking. Haohua Yuhang, a subsidiary of state-owned chemical giant Sinochem Holdings, has entered the trial production stage for ultra-high-purity hydrogen chloride, according to a report from Science and Technology Daily.Reportedly, the facility achieved good results on its very first run. Testing confirmed that the gas reached a purity level exceeding 99.9999 percent, with total impurities capped at no more than 0.2 parts per million.Silicon wafers serve as the foundation for modern electronics, so keeping them spotless ensures that subsequent manufacturing stages remain accurate.Key microchip chemicalMicrochips are the essential brains, memory, and control systems for nearly all modern electronics. With the rising demand for these devices, it has become important to maintain material purity during manufacturing.Semiconductor manufacturers depend on ultra-high-purity hydrogen chloride gas to clean and prepare silicon wafers at a microscopic scale.When this gas reacts with silicon or trace metals, it converts the impurities into gaseous byproducts that are easily pumped out of the reaction chamber without leaving any physical residue. This selective chemical action removes surface imperfections and native oxides, and leaves the underlying silicon crystal undamaged. This entire process leaves the wafer completely smooth, and new layers form properly without defects.Standard hydrogen chloride is a common industrial chemical. Refining it to electronic grade requires an entirely different level of precision. So achieving a purity level exceeding 99.9999 percent is a major chemical engineering challenge. Standard industrial HCl contains trace amounts of moisture, nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, and various chlorosilanes. To drop total impurities below 0.2 parts per million, producers use specialized fractional distillation columns made of high-grade, corrosion-resistant alloys. They also use advanced cryogenic and adsorption purification systems to filter out even molecular-level contaminants.For those strict semiconductor standards, the Sinochem project team redesigned its distillation and purification methods, making multiple technical adjustments before finalizing the production process.China boosts domestic supplySemiconductor fabs depend on this ultra-pure gas for several delicate steps in wafer fabrication. Technicians use it to polish silicon wafers, etch microscopic patterns, and treat surfaces before growing new semiconductor layers. International semiconductor supply chains depend on specialized chemical inputs to keep production lines running smoothly. Reports also suggest hydrogen chloride as a vital specialty gas within this global manufacturing network. Without steady access to these high-purity materials, chipmakers cannot sustain the complex fabrication processes needed for modern electronics.China already hosts domestic suppliers in this niche market, including Zhejiang-based specialty gas producer GrandiT Technology. Still, the arrival of a state-backed powerhouse like Sinochem adds significant muscle to the country’s homegrown capacity.For now, the Haohua Yuhang facility remains in its trial phase. Scaling up from successful initial tests to continuous, commercial-grade output will be the next big hurdle for China’s semiconductor material ambitions.Ongoing research and development continue to advance quality control in the semiconductor gas sector. For example, the Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS) established purity testing procedures for 15 high-purity semiconductor gases, along with six certified reference materials. These standardized tools allow manufacturers to verify measurement precision and maintain strict quality standards accurately.

title: New radio system cuts EV wireless charging alignment error by 80%
content: A radio system based on the technology used in some digital car keys cut the median error in locating an electric vehicle’s wireless charging coil by about 80 percent after researchers corrected for signal distortions in a lab test.The system estimates where the coil sits relative to a charging pad and which way the vehicle is facing.Researchers at the University of Osaka in Japan developed the system with Tokai Rika and the University of California, San Diego. They tested it on a scaled-down vehicle model using ultra-wideband (UWB) signals to measure the coil’s position. Why parking position mattersWireless EV chargers send power from a pad on the ground to a receiver coil mounted underneath the vehicle. Shifting the coil a few centimeters away from the center of the pad or parking at the wrong angle can reduce the efficiency of the power transfer. That can leave the vehicle sitting on the pad longer to get the same amount of charge.Magnetic positioning systems generally work best once the coil is already close to the pad. Cameras can help guide parking, but rain, dirt, or poor lighting can make it harder for them to see the pad.The researchers used radio measurements to estimate both the coil’s location and the angle of the vehicle.How the radio signals locate the coilThe team placed four UWB devices around the model’s receiver coil and set up antennas near the charging pad. The devices exchanged short-range radio signals with the antennas. The system first measured how long the signals took to travel between them to get a rough fix on the vehicle’s location.It then compared the phase of the waves as they arrived at different devices. Those small differences let the system refine its estimate of the coil’s position and the direction the vehicle was pointing. The researchers also measured distortions specific to the installation in advance and used those measurements to correct the readings.What the lab test showedThe team took repeated measurements with the model stopped in one position. With the correction applied, the median error in the estimated vehicle angle was 0.25 degrees. The median error in the estimated coil position was roughly five times as large when the researchers left the correction out.The researchers showed how the position and angle readings could be displayed to guide a vehicle over the pad. The approach could also help robotaxis and other autonomous EVs line up to recharge without someone on hand to plug them in.“Turning a computational method into a working system required considerable trial and error. We hope this research will lead to a future where EVs charge simply by parking, much like smartphones placed on wireless chargers,” said Ryotaro Hada, the first author of the study.The system still needs to be tested outdoors, on full-sized vehicles and while a charger is transferring power.The study was published in the IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology.

title: Chinese robot handles hotel laundry workflow in just 18.6 seconds
content: China-based ACE Robotics has demonstrated a hotel laundry workflow using its Mundo world model, combining robotic skills with cloud-based planning to automate the process from collection to delivery. The system enables a robot to collect laundry baskets from guest rooms, transport them to a laundry room, operate washing machines and dryers, and return clean clothes.Mundo creates interactive digital twins of hotel environments from photographs, allowing robots to simulate tasks and learn how objects behave before operating in the real world.According to the company, a self-improving skills system uses feedback from real-world failures to refine performance, bringing the complete laundry workflow down to 18.6 seconds.Robots master laundryThe Mundo system allows a robot to collect laundry baskets from guest rooms, transport them to a laundry room, operate washing machines and dryers, and return the clean clothes. The demonstration marks the first long-chain commercial application of Mundo since ACE Robotics and Nanyang Technological University’s S-Lab introduced the world model last month.At the center of the system is Mundo, which converts photographs of hotel rooms, corridors, and laundry facilities into interactive digital twins. Unlike conventional visual simulations, these environments incorporate physical properties such as object mass and friction, allowing robots to learn how objects respond to contact and movement.Each simulation produces data on robot trajectories, contact states, and visual feedback. This information helps refine the robot’s action policies before it attempts the same tasks in a real hotel environment.ACE Robotics uses a dual-model architecture to divide complex planning from real-time execution. A general-purpose cloud model, identified by QbitAI as GPT-Astra, handles task decomposition, reasoning, and strategy exploration inside Mundo. Once the system identifies a workable approach, it stores the procedure as a reusable robotic skill. A separate model running locally on the robot then retrieves and executes these skills to perform individual actions.The division is intended to avoid the delays associated with relying on cloud computing for every movement. ACE Robotics said its cloud-based approach took more than 30 minutes to complete a full laundry run, while the local execution model reduced the time to 18.648 seconds.A scheduling system called BotAgent coordinates the workflow, dividing laundry operations into 53 atomic actions and 14 higher-level semantic steps. It can arrange more than 200 possible action sequences based on factors such as room locations, elevator availability, and queues at washing machines.Robots learn from failureThe system also incorporates a feedback loop designed to improve robotic skills through repeated real-world attempts. When an operation fails, the cloud model examines multi-camera footage and sensor logs to identify what went wrong. It can then propose changes to the robot’s movements or select alternative camera views to overcome visibility problems.In one example, the system switched to an overhead camera after the robot’s wrist-mounted camera became obstructed. In another, it modified the gripper’s lifting trajectory and fingertip angles after jeans became caught inside a dryer drum.The robot can also reset the environment autonomously between attempts. A separate model evaluates each round, allowing the system to retain better-performing skill versions and roll back less effective changes.For dryer unloading alone, ACE Robotics reported conducting 165 real-robot trials over 57 hours. These produced 37 improvement proposals and approximately 80 skill versions. The company said unloading cycles eventually settled at 170 to 210 seconds. The average proportion of jeans left inside the dryer fell from 48 percent to 32 percent, with the best recorded run reaching 19 percent.ACE Robotics identified instant retail as another potential application for the technology. However, the reported performance figures come from the company and have not been independently verified.
